notes.text:
# Independent reconstruction and current-proof audit

This note audits the actual native277 FINAL and the five DIFFERENT expanded notes, rather than treating either as an incoming correctness grant. There are no incoming note grants. The conclusions below are independently derived under the published foundations explicitly stated here. The analytic and calibration foundations are conventional source theorems; their deeper proof trees are not claimed freshly proved.

Put K=C((s)), |s|=exp(-1/8), t=s^8, Y=(G_m^2)^an, Lambda=< (t,2),(3,t) >, and X=Y/Lambda. Write x_i=-log|z_i|. The periods translate x by Z^2. Open tropical rectangles of widths less than one have disjoint nonidentity translates and give an ordinary open torus atlas on X. The compact polyannulus x^(-1)([0,1]^2) surjects onto X. On bounded tropical boxes only finitely many deck graphs meet; each is closed. A finite cover by injective quotient charts gives a flat quasi-finite analytic surjection with finite fibres, as does its product cover. Descent of the relation's coherent ideal makes the diagonal closed. The charts are smooth and boundaryless; strict affinoid neighbourhoods exist by choosing rational radii in the divisible value group. Thus X is compact, Hausdorff, separated, good, strict, smooth, connected and pure of dimension two, and is proper. This does not invoke quasi-finite descent for the infinite-sheeted map Y->X.

The exact conventional descent inputs are Conrad--Temkin, Non-archimedean analytification of algebraic spaces, Lemma4.2.3 (an etale relation whose restrictions to an ordinary open cover have quotients has a quotient, covered by the resulting open quotients), Lemma4.2.4 (coherent G-sheaves descend along a flat quasi-finite analytic surjection), and the subsequent coherent-ideal closed-immersion argument. Their complete immediate proofs were read. Theorem2.3.1 reflects separatedness, smoothness and, for finite-type maps, properness under analytification. Its immediate proof and Example2.3.2 at closed points were also read. None provides a field-extension rule for the energy or arbitrary current identities.

Here is the nonalgebraization check. Gruson IV.5 Theorem1 gives SK^0(H)=0 for completed products of disc algebras with radii in the divisible value group and unit-circle algebras. Determinants of a stable equality trivialize rank-one projective modules. For wide annulus factors use induction: trivialize a line bundle on its inner circle times the remaining factors, glue it to the trivial bundle on the inner disc, and fill the annulus to the outer disc. The rational cover has intersection exactly the inner circle. Tate--Kiehl coherent gluing, as stated in Van der Put2.14--2.16.3, is the conventional foundation here. This proves Pic(P_m)=0 for P_m={|s|^m<=|z_i|<=|s|^(-m)}; it does not apply Gruson directly to wide annuli.

For a unit b=sum b_beta z^beta on P_m, its Gauss log norm and that of its inverse are convex and opposite, hence affine. A maximizing monomial at an interior tropical point agrees with that affine norm on the whole box. Its exponent alpha gives |b_beta/b_alpha|exp((m/8)|beta-alpha|_1)<=1. Thus b=b_alpha z^alpha(1+g) and ||g||_(P_j)<=|s|^(m-j) for j<m. A global unit on Y is a scalar monomial, since any distinct exponent would dominate along a ray. Normalize consecutive frames by scalar monomials to have e_(m+1)=(1+g_m)e_m. On fixed P_j the products product_(m>=j)(1+g_m) and their inverse tails converge; the frames patched by these products agree on overlaps. Hence Pic(Y)=0.

Equivariant multipliers have the form c_i z^(h_i). Writing h_1=(A,B), h_2=(C,D), their commutativity gives t^C 2^D=3^A t^B. Therefore C=B and A=D=0, and h_1=(0,k), h_2=(k,0). If k is nonzero choose lambda=lambda_1 lambda_2^(sign k); its multiplier exponent h=(k sign k,k) has v(lambda^h)=2|k|>0. A section satisfying f(lambda z)=c z^h f(z) has coefficients a_(m+jh)=a_m c^j lambda^(-jm-hj(j+1)/2). Their valuations have negative quadratic leading term, contradicting convergence on the unit polyannulus. If k=0 the two period equations force any two nonzero exponents to coincide. Every nonzero section is then a nowhere-zero monomial, and two sections with the same multipliers are proportional.

For a meromorphic F the pole ideal J={b:bF is analytic} is locally the kernel of multiplication by a numerator into O/(denominator). Regular-local factoriality makes it invertible; flat analytic restrictions commute with the kernel. Stacks0AG0 states that a regular local ring is a UFD. Ducros, Families of Berkovich spaces2.1.3(2),(5), gives regularity of affinoid-domain and analytic-local restriction maps, and2.1.4 gives regularity of algebraic-to-analytic local maps. These exact statements, with their references to deeper foundations, were read. Trivialize J on Y. Its frame and its product with F are two analytic sections with the same deck multipliers; the preceding computation makes F constant. Thus Gamma(X,M_X)=K. If X=Z^an for a separated finite-type K-algebraic space, reflection makes Z smooth proper connected and therefore integral of dimension two. Stacks086U gives a dense scheme locus for a decent space;0BB1 gives the equivalent finiteness of irreducible components on quasi-compact etale charts;0EN6/0ENA identify meromorphic and rational functions when weak associates have codimension zero and the generic points are field monomorphisms;0END identifies the resulting integral function field. These hypotheses hold for smooth separated finite-type Z. Their statements and immediate proofs were read. Flat analytic local maps preserve denominators, and a closed point in a scheme open avoiding zeros detects nonzero rational functions. Thus K(Z), of transcendence degree two, injects into Gamma(X,M_X)=K, a contradiction. No claim is made that nonalgebraizability persists after every field extension.

Set rho=|x|^2/2 and theta=DD rho, DD=d'd''. Deck changes are smooth affine unit-logarithms. The conventional CLD identity-torus integration rule, with saturated lattice Z^2, analytic degree one and factor2!, gives theta^2=2 i_*dx on the Gauss section of the unit tropical torus. The raw mass is M=2. This calibrated rule is a named foundation, not a new recursive calibration audit. Theta vanishes on a residue bidisc; it is not globally strictly positive.

Let P be the minimal continuous CLD psh sheaf, closed under uniform limits, and C={u in C(X):rho+u belongs locally to P}. The precise CLDv2 foundations are Definition8.1.7/Lemma8.1.8; multiplier convergence8.5.1; smooth closed-factor differentiation8.5.3; positivity and closedness of DD(fT) for continuous psh f and positive closed T,8.5.5; recursive products8.7.1, their local uniform continuity8.7.2, symmetry8.7.4, and continuous dpsh extension and smooth DD-null changes8.8.4--5. Proposition7.2.8 identifies positive top currents with Radon measures on locally differentially separated spaces;7.2.11--12 provides coefficient measures. Smooth Stokes/Green5.11.1 has analytic boundary terms;15.7.1 equips a separated pure-dimensional analytic space with the compatible tropical calculus. All applied statements and immediate proofs were read in corrected literal-LF units. The boundary here is empty. Smooth cutoffs, partitions, scalar approximation, underlying positivity and calibrated integration remain conventional foundations. No use is made of the problematic arbitrary-multiplier closedness assertion8.6.7 or of equality with the first approximation stage.

Convex and finite-max closure of C holds at all stages: prove the operations for smooth psh weights, using convex soft maxima, then fix one smooth slot and apply minimality to the other slot's uniform-closed sheaf; fix that resulting slot and repeat in the remaining slot. Constants belong to C. For u,v in C, theta_u=theta+DD[u] and B(u,v)=theta wedge theta_v+DD(u theta_v) are the actual symmetric positive local bounded products. They glue by smooth affine potential changes and have mass two by testing exact terms with1. MA(u)=B(u,u).

For completeness the additional Green step can be reconstructed without first-stage approximation. Fix positive closed (1,1) T and complete compact smooth (1,0) forms for the positive semidefinite pairing integral a wedge Jb wedge T. On patches use Q_(T,chi) with nonnegative smooth compact chi. Uniformly smooth approximable functions with strongly converging gradients form a sheaf H_T: partitions patch their approximants by the Leibniz rule; products and cutoffs obey the same rule. Bounded continuous coefficients act by scalar approximation and the bound ||fa||<=||f||_infinity||a||. A uniformly zero sequence with a strong gradient limit has zero limit gradient, since closedness gives integral d'f_j wedge Jb wedge T=-integral f_j d'(Jb) wedge T->0 against every smooth b, a dense set of Hilbert tests. Larger-patch cutoffs give the local assertion.

If f belongs to H_T and L_T f=DD(fT) is signed Radon, smooth approximation first in f and then in a compactly supported g gives integral g L_Tf=-Q_T(f,g). Consequently Q_(T,chi)(w,w)=1/2 integral w^2 DDchi wedge T-integral chi w L_Tw. The sheaf {f in H_T:L_Tf>=0} contains smooth psh functions. For f_j uniformly convergent there, choose nested cutoffs chi,eta with eta=1 near supp chi and |f_j|<=B on the WHOLE supp eta. Put epsilon=||f_j-f_k|| there. Positivity and the displayed identity give

0<=Q_(T,chi)(f_j-f_k)<=epsilon^2 ||DDchi wedge T||_TV/2+2B epsilon ||chi||_infinity ||DDeta wedge T||_TV.

The gradients are strongly Cauchy; choose local smooth approximants with uniform and cutoff-gradient errors below1/j. Distributional positivity survives. Minimality places every stage of P in this sheaf. Finite patching on X therefore proves integral f DD(gT)=integral g DD(fT)=-Q_T(f,g), with Q_T(f,f)>=0, for continuous dpsh f,g.

Define E(u)=1/3 integral u[MA(0)+B(u,0)+MA(u)]. Differentiating this cubic, and using Green with theta and theta_(u_t), yields dE(u_t)/dt=integral(v-u)MA(u_t) and d^2E(u_t)/dt^2=-2Q_(theta_(u_t))(v-u)<=0. Hence E is monotone, concave, E(0)=0, E(u+c)=E(u)+2c, and obeys the tangent inequality. Integrating the quadratic Bernstein coefficients gives E(u)-E(v)=1/3 integral(u-v)[MA(u)+B(u,v)+MA(v)]. If u>=v each nonnegative integral is at most3(E(u)-E(v)). For bounded comparison, put m=max(u,v-epsilon). Locality on the two strict ordinary open comparison sets and mass2 give MA(v){u<v-epsilon}<=MA(u){u<=v-epsilon}. Both increasing unions as epsilon decreases to zero equal {u<v}; continuity from below proves the strict comparison inequality, retaining every contact atom on the correct side.

Let G be the ACTUAL pointwise limits u_j downarrow u, u_j in C, inf E(u_j)>-infinity. These are USC. Energy is canonical for every continuous decreasing presentation: if v_j downarrow u and continuous a strictly dominates u everywhere, the open sets {v_j<a} increase and cover compact X, so one index works globally. Compare each presentation to a term of the other plus epsilon and reverse the roles. Monotonicity and the constant rule give the same finite energy limit. The same argument gives generated order preservation. An identically -infinite limit would eventually be below every negative constant and contradict the energy bound. Convexity and concavity pass to G.

On any finite simplex of generated weights, bounded energies are polynomials of degree at most three. Values converge at a finite unisolvent set in the simplex, so their coefficients converge and give the canonical energy polynomial everywhere. A nonzero polynomial cannot vanish on an open simplex, proving existence of that interpolation set. Zero coefficient weights are omitted at endpoints. At this point the elementary energy-continuity proof applies when a decreasing generated sequence has an already generated limit; n2 below removes that prerequisite for energy-bounded SEQUENCES by proving actual representability.

For a positive finite Radon measure set E*(mu)=sup_(v in C)(E(v)-integral v mu). Constants force mu(X)=2 if this is finite. Shift a presentation below zero and use monotone convergence to get integral(-u)mu<=E*(mu)-E(u) for u<=0, finite integrability and L1 convergence of every continuous decreasing presentation. Generated pole sets are mu-null. Bounded tangent gives E*(MA(v))=E(v)-integral v MA(v).

The generated operator follows from actual bounded products, not a dual inverse. For any presentation u_j downarrow u and v in C let P_j(t)=E((1-t)u_j+tv), R_j(t)=E(tu_j). Cubic coefficient convergence and bounded first variation give integral v MA(u_j)=P'_j(0)+R'_j(1), whose limit is presentation-independent. The span D of C is uniformly dense in C(X). To check this, different tropical classes are separated by small smooth periodic perturbations of rho. In one tropical fibre distinct seminorms differ on a Laurent polynomial P. In a lift chart |x_i-a_i|<r<1/2, choose delta<r^2/4 and epsilon small so delta+epsilon(log|P|-b)<rho_a on a tropical boundary collar, where b=log|P(p)| and rho_a=|x-a|^2/2. The function max(rho_a,delta+epsilon(log|P|-b))-rho_a, extended by zero, is continuous theta-psh and separates p,q. Near zeros it equals zero; elsewhere soft maxima apply. D is a vector lattice: for differences with common scale A, max(A(p-q),A(r-s))=2A max((p+s)/2,(r+q)/2)-A(q+s). The finite-cover lattice approximation argument proves density. Positive common mass then extends convergence from D to ALL continuous tests. Compact-Hausdorff Riesz representation gives a unique Radon MA(u) of mass two. Polarization gives positive presentation-independent mixed limits B(u,v).

Here are the moment steps that are essential to the audit. D_u=lim integral u_j MA(u_j) is the coefficient R'(1). Tangent gives E*(MA(u))<=E(u)-D_u<infinity. This first establishes integrability. For k>=j the bounded cocycle gives 0<=integral(u_j-u_k)MA(u_k)<=3(E(u_j)-E(u_k)). Let k then j tend to infinity, using the fixed continuous test u_j and the newly established L1 convergence. It follows that D_u=integral u MA(u) and E*(MA(u))=E(u)-integral u MA(u). No unbounded moment was presumed to obtain finite dual.

For F(t,s)=E(tu+sw), partial_s F(1,0)=integral w MA(u). First use bounded w. Then decrease bounded w_l to w; at each simplex point the limit is already the convex generated tu+sw, so energy continuity and interpolation give coefficient convergence, while finite dual gives L1 convergence. Multivariate substitution gives the actual generated first variation along every segment. Applying coefficients to generated decreasing families with generated limits yields weak operator convergence and integral u_j MA(v_j)->integral u MA(v), as well as the fixed-u version. Subtracting gives the moving estimate integral |u_j-u| MA(v_j)->0. Polarization gives mixed moments and bounds B(a,b)<=2 MA((a+b)/2).

To pass comparison and locality on possibly nonopen sets, first replace a_j-b_j by a-b in bounded Lipschitz tests using moving L1. Then replace by fixed continuous a_l-b_l using fixed-slot moment convergence; use weak convergence at fixed l; finally let l tend to infinity. At an atom-free level, Lipschitz ramps give indicator convergence. There are at most countably many bad levels. This proves MA(v){u<v}<=MA(u){u<v} and 1_(u>v) MA(max(u,v))=1_(u>v)MA(u). Polarization gives mixed max locality. Finite Borel restrictions of finite Radon measures on compact Hausdorff X remain regular, so continuous-test equality identifies the restrictions. Thus for u<=0, u^A=max(u,-A),

1_(u>-A) MA(u^A)=1_(u>-A)MA(u),

and these restrictions increase to MA(u) of mass two. The ENTIRE contact set u=-A is excluded. If E(u)>=-C, the discarded mass is <=3C/A, by E*(MA(u^A))<=2C and the finite-dual bound. Mixed restrictions with u>-A,v>-B are exact and have discarded mass <=2(2C_u+C_v)/A+2(C_u+2C_v)/B. These are generated products; bounded discontinuous clamps are not silently identified with preexisting continuous CLD products.

The independent audit finds no missing step in this scoped generated chain under the stated conventional foundations. It does not turn the chain into intrinsic E1 recognition, arbitrary-support existence, pointwise uniqueness, or energy-sublevel compactness. Actual finite moments, raw mass, every presentation and nonopen indicator passage are essential limitations, not optional conventions. The source/reading evidence and the distinctions among the three serializations are recorded in n5 and source-application-reading-ledger.md. The complete standalone reconstruction is in scoped-paper.tex and proof-companion.md. No supplied program or old verdict is used as a premise.

notes.summary: New actual countable closure: every decreasing generated sequence with a common finite lower energy bound has a continuous decreasing presentation of its exact pointwise limit; energy converges.
notes.detailedSummary: A constrained global diagonal enumerates all inner continuous terms, stays below finitely many of them up to2^-n and below its predecessor up to2^-n, and adds the summable tail. Compact strict dominance works for USC outer terms even at poles. The resulting presentation has the exact original pointwise infimum and retains the energy bound. Countable downward directed infima follow; arbitrary net compactness is not claimed.

# Countable monotone closure with an actual analytic presentation

New theorem. On the analytic carrier, positivity datum and generated domain G reconstructed in n1, suppose u_k in G decrease pointwise and inf_k E(u_k)>-infinity. Then their ACTUAL pointwise limit u belongs to G and E(u_k) decreases to E(u). The hypothesis that the limit is already generated is unnecessary for sequences with this energy bound. No metrizability, countable point set, strictness of theta, or arbitrary-current base change is required. This is countable monotone closure, not compactness of an arbitrary sublevel net.

I give the diagonal construction explicitly; it is more than a choice of matching indices in the presentations. Choose presentations f_(k,j) in C, f_(k,j) downarrow u_k. Each continuous term is bounded on compact X; no uniform lower bound on the entire presentation is assumed. Enumerate ALL pairs (k,j) as a sequence, and denote the resulting continuous functions by h_1,h_2,... . Thus inf_m h_m=u pointwise. Every h_m dominates u. Fix epsilon_n=2^(-n), set r_n=sum_(ell>n) epsilon_ell=2^(-n), and initialize k_0=0.

The compactness lemma needed here holds even for USC outer terms: if g_k downarrow g, each g_k is USC, and a is finite continuous with g<a everywhere, then {g_k<a} is an increasing ordinary open cover of compact X. A finite subcover gives a global late index. This statement includes poles and uses strict inequality.

At stage n choose k_n>=max(n,k_(n-1)) so that

u_(k_n)<h_m+epsilon_n everywhere for all m<=n.

This is possible by the compactness lemma applied to the continuous minimum of the finitely many h_m+epsilon_n. That minimum is only a bound: it is NEVER inserted into the psh class. For n>1, u_(k_n)<=u_(k_(n-1))<=v_(n-1), so u_(k_n)<v_(n-1)+epsilon_n also holds. Apply the same lemma to the continuous presentation of u_(k_n). Select j_n such that v_n=f_(k_n,j_n) satisfies, everywhere,

v_n<h_m+epsilon_n (m<=n), and v_n<v_(n-1)+epsilon_n (n>1).

There are finitely many strict bounds at this stage, so one j_n works. Now put a_n=v_n+r_n. Constants preserve C, and

a_n-a_(n-1)<epsilon_n+r_n-r_(n-1)=0.

Thus a_n in C is decreasing. It dominates u. For fixed m and n>=m it is <h_m+epsilon_n+r_n, so its limit a is <=h_m for every m. Therefore a<=inf_m h_m=u. Combining both inequalities gives a=u pointwise, including every pole. This is a single genuine continuous analytic presentation of the original limit; it is not an abstract functional representative or an equality modulo a null set.

Let L=inf_k E(u_k)>-infinity. Since v_n>=u_(k_n), generated order preservation in n1 gives E(v_n)>=E(u_(k_n))>=L. The constant rule gives E(a_n)>=L. Hence the new presentation has finite lower energy and u belongs to G. Its upper energy is finite because its first term is continuous. The non-bottom conclusion of n1 applies, so u cannot be identically -infinity.

There is also an explicit check of the energy limit. Order gives E(u)<=E(u_k), so E(u)<=L. For any fixed continuous presentation term b_l downarrow u and eta>0, the open sets {u_k<b_l+eta} increase and cover X. The compactness lemma gives E(u_k)<=E(b_l)+2eta for large k. Taking k to infinity, then l to infinity and eta to zero, gives L<=E(u). Thus E(u_k) downarrow E(u), without circular use of continuity to prove generation.

The proof uses only compactness, USC outer terms, continuous presentations, constant stability, canonical monotone energy, and its positive mass constant rule. Its analytic applicability follows from the independent bounded-current/energy reconstruction in n1; no earlier supplied note is a premise. A naive diagonal would be wrong even on one point: f_(k,j)=0 for j<2^k and f_(k,j)=-1+1/k otherwise decreases in j to u_k=-1+1/k. The u_k decrease to -1 and have uniformly bounded energies for E(c)=2c, but f_(k,k) converges to0. The finitely many GLOBAL upper constraints above are exactly what prevents that failure.

Corollary. A countable downward directed family of members of G with a common lower energy bound has its pointwise infimum in G. Recursively choose a member below the previously chosen member and the next enumerated member. This produces a decreasing sequence coinitial in the family, to which the theorem applies. An uncountable decreasing net is covered only if it admits such a countable coinitial reduction (or another independently proved representation theorem). The construction does not provide one automatically.

Artifacts: n2.md contains the full proof; scoped-paper.tex and proof-companion.md integrate it with the independent bounded and generated foundations. The theorem proves an actual countable closure gate on the genuine analytic space. Separated normalized energy-sublevel compactness and full P16.7 remain unresolved.

# Ordered operator continuity and infinite convex sums

The following are new consequences of n1 and the actual countable presentation theorem n2. They impose no invariance or support restriction.

If u_k in G decrease and inf E(u_k)>-infinity, then u=inf u_k is generated by n2. The canonical energy continuity now applies with a proved actual limit. For every v in C, the coefficients of E((1-t)u_k+tv) and E(tu_k) converge by finite interpolation, and their boundary derivative identity from n1 gives integral v MA(u_k)->integral v MA(u). Density of span C and mass two give weak convergence against EVERY continuous analytic-space test. Polarization gives B(u_k,v_k)->B(u,v) if both decreasing families have finite lower energy bounds. This extends the previously conditional decreasing operator theorem to all such sequences; it does not assert general net convergence.

There is actual L1 convergence for arbitrary-support finite-full-dual measures. Let mu be positive Radon, mu(X)=2 and D=E*(mu)<infinity. The potentials u_k and u are integrable by n1, and u_1 dominates every u_k. Their decreasing differences u_k-u are nonnegative and bounded above mu-a.e. by the integrable u_1-u. Dominated convergence gives integral |u_k-u|mu->0. Moving MA moments and mixed moments follow exactly from the multivariate energy coefficients in n1, because n2 has now proved their limiting potentials generated. In particular, integral |u_k-u|MA(v_k)->0 for any second energy-bounded decreasing generated sequence v_k. These facts concern each ordered family and do not assert uniform integrability of a whole nonordered energy sublevel.

Here is a further actual analytic closure theorem. Suppose u_i in G are nonpositive, E(u_i)>=-C_i with C_i>=0, and t_i>=0 satisfy T=sum t_i<=1 and C_tot=sum t_i C_i<infinity. Omit zero coefficients, especially at poles. Define s_N=sum_(i<=N)t_i u_i and u=sum_(i>=1)t_i u_i pointwise, in R union {-infinity}. Each s_N is the finite convex combination of the u_i and zero with remaining coefficient 1-sum_(i<=N)t_i. Convexity gives s_N in G and concavity gives E(s_N)>=-sum_(i<=N)t_i C_i>=-C_tot. Because each u_i<=0, s_N decreases to the prescribed pointwise sum u. The theorem n2 supplies a single bounded continuous analytic decreasing presentation of that exact sum. Thus u in G, E(u)>=-C_tot, E(s_N) downarrow E(u), MA(s_N)->MA(u), and the sum is USC. It is not identically -infinity.

For every finite-full-dual mu as above, Tonelli and the n1 dual bound give an exact quantitative tail estimate:

integral |s_N-u|mu=sum_(i>N)t_i integral(-u_i)mu
<=D sum_(i>N)t_i+sum_(i>N)t_i C_i ->0.

All terms are nonnegative, so no undefined difference of infinite integrals occurs. On the common mu-null union of pole sets and the pole set of the sum, values of the differences may be assigned arbitrarily. This proves integrability and control for a fixed summable family, with the actual representative supplied independently by n2. It does not replace analytic potentials by an inverse Banach measure.

For completeness, the finite-dual variational objective over G equals its supremum over C: for any u in G its bounded continuous presentation satisfies E(a_j)-integral a_j mu->E(u)-integral u mu. Hence enlarging to these actual countable completions changes neither E*(mu) nor the eligible measure condition. Constants still fix the raw mass two. This is a noncircular necessary condition; none of the closure theorems proves that every such mu is MA(u).

Artifacts: n3.md, scoped-paper.tex and proof-companion.md contain the complete proofs. The newly constructed limits are actual analytic generated potentials. General energy-sublevel compactness, obstacle orthogonality, arbitrary-support equation existence and full uniqueness are separate remaining gates.

# All-test separation, classical recognition, and the unresolved uniqueness step

This note independently checks the entire current all-test argument and ROOT394/395. It uses the bounded and generated calculus proved in n1; the new countable closure and its consequences are n2 and n3. The published curve and classical-psh results are stated at their retained hypotheses below. No old positive verdict is a premise.

For continuous dpsh functions write $Q_T(f,h)=-\int fDD(hT)$, with the positive Hilbert pairing of n1 when $T$ is positive closed. Put $f=a-b$, $g=(a+b)/2$, $h=w-g$, and $I(a,b)=\int(a-b)[MA(b)-MA(a)]$. Bounded expansion and Green give
\[
 I(a,b)=Q_{\theta_a}(f,f)+Q_{\theta_b}(f,f)\geq0.
\]
The signed transgression is
\[
 Q_{\theta_w}(f,f)-Q_{\theta_g}(f,f)
 =Q_{\theta_a}(f,h)-Q_{\theta_b}(f,h).
\]
Both sides equal $-\int fDDf\wedge DDh$ by the symmetric continuous dpsh product and $DDf=\theta_a-\theta_b$. Thus Cauchy--Schwarz in the two positive current slots gives
\[
 Q_{\theta_w}(f,f)\leq I(a,b)/2+
 \sqrt{I(a,b)(Q_{\theta_a}(h,h)+Q_{\theta_b}(h,h))}.
\]

Normalize $a,b,w\leq0$ and assume $E(a),E(b),E(w)\geq-C$. The dual estimate in n1 gives $\int(-p)MA(q)\leq3C$ for any two of these weights. Since $B(q,r)\leq2MA((q+r)/2)$, concavity and the same estimate give $\int(-p)B(q,r)\leq6C$. From $|h|\leq-w+(-a-b)/2$ follow $\int|h|MA(q)\leq6C$ and $\int|h|B(q,r)\leq12C$. Expanding
\[
 Q_{\theta_a}(h,h)
 =-\int h\left[B(a,w)-(MA(a)+B(a,b))/2\right]
\]
bounds this slot by $12C+3C+6C=21C$; the other slot has the same bound. Consequently
\[
 Q_{\theta_w}(a-b,a-b)\leq I(a,b)/2+\sqrt{42C I(a,b)}.
\]
This estimate tests every bounded continuous $w\in\mathcal C$, rather than just the degenerate reference current.

If generated $u,v$ have equal MA, choose any continuous decreasing presentations and subtract fixed upper constants. Their energies have a common lower bound. The four moving moments from n1 show $I(u_j,v_j)\to0$, so $Q_{\theta_w}(u_j-v_j,u_j-v_j)\to0$ for every fixed bounded test. For $u,v\in\mathcal C$ themselves the same estimate gives zero pairing. Green and Cauchy--Schwarz against compact smooth scalar tests imply $DD((u-v)\theta_w)=0$.

Here is the exact bounded divisor consequence. In a lift torus chart put $\rho_a=|x-a|^2/2$. Let $P$ be a nonzero Laurent polynomial and $\chi$ a smooth convex function, zero on $(-\infty,0]$, with $0\leq\chi'\leq1$ and $\chi(t)=t-c$ for $t\geq1$. The capped function $\psi_N=\chi(\log|P|+N)$ is ordinary smooth and psh: it is locally zero at zeros of $P$, and elsewhere is a smooth convex unit-logarithm function. Choose $0<\delta<r^2/4$ on a chart $|x_i-a_i|<r$, and a positive $\varepsilon_N$ sufficiently small to make
\[
 w_N=\max(\rho_a,\delta+\varepsilon_N\psi_N)-\rho_a
\]
zero on a tropical boundary collar. Its zero extension is in $\mathcal C$. On the fixed inner neighbourhood $\rho_a<\delta/2$ its curvature equals $\varepsilon_N DD\psi_N$.

CLDv2 Theorem16.7.3 is the Poincare--Lelong identity $DD[\log|P|]=\delta_{\operatorname{div}P}$ for a regular meromorphic function on a boundaryless pure-dimensional analytic space. The whole applied statement and immediate proof were read in LF23458--23671, including its Stokes, boundary and calibration steps. The torus chart is smooth and boundaryless and nonzero holomorphic $P$ is regular. Compact smooth top-test supports avoid the lower-dimensional divisor, so $[\psi_N-N]$ is eventually $[\log|P|-c]$ there. Hence $DD\psi_N\to\delta_{\operatorname{div}P}$. Continuous multiplier convergence CLD8.5.1, used ONLY for bounded continuous $u-v$, gives
\[
 DD((u-v)\delta_{\operatorname{div}P})=0
\]
on that fixed inner neighbourhood. This is an ambient divisor-current identity. It is not an unbounded restriction or a proof of curve harmonicity for every analytic curve.

The newer classical bridge is valid, with the following exact source scope. Gubler--Rabinoff, Classically psh and pluriharmonic functions on Berkovich spaces, arXiv:2506.13548v2, 17 September2025, Definition4.1 tests ALL analytic curves after ALL analytic complete field extensions. Definition3.4 uses separated pure-dimensional analytic curves over nontrivially valued fields and includes the identically-minus-infinite alternative. Theorem1.2 already proves the ordinary smooth CLD-to-classical psh implication; this is published input, not a new contribution. Theorem4.2 supplies the sheaf, convex/max and decreasing-net closure properties, analytic pullback and field-extension functoriality. The full applied units and immediate proofs were read, including the source's reductions and dependencies. Their deeper proof trees remain named foundations.

One can therefore prove the ALL-stage continuous recognition without assuming a first-stage identity. On a compact neighbourhood take classical psh $h_j$ uniformly approaching continuous $h$, and pass to a subsequence with error at most $2^{-j}$. Then $g_j=h_j+3\cdot2^{-j}$ decreases: $h_{j+1}-h_j\leq 3\cdot2^{-j-1}$, precisely the decrease of the added constants. Its limit is $h$. The source's decreasing closure proves uniform closure of the finite continuous classical sheaf. Minimality places the complete continuous CLD sheaf P in it. Hence every generated local weight $\rho+u$ is classically psh, including at poles, by the same decreasing closure. The new limits and infinite sums from n2--n3 are thus actual classically psh analytic representatives.

The source's Theorem6.4 states the affinoid Shilov maximum principle for an USC classical psh function, with arbitrary complete fields and affinoid radii: $\max_A q=\max_{\Gamma_A}q$ for affinoid $A$. Its complete immediate proof uses Theorem6.1 (local maximum), Lemma5.4 (curve connectivity) and Proposition6.3 (boundary strata); all were read. On original PDF page33 the proof calls $q$ continuous, but the closed maximum set needed there is also closed for USC $q$, the stated hypothesis. Original pages3,33,34 were viewed. This repairs that wording locally without strengthening the theorem's hypothesis.

Here are independently checked consequences, not a fixed skeleton assertion. For every point and all arbitrarily small affinoid neighbourhoods contained in a local weight chart,
\[
 q(x)=\inf_{A\ni x\text{ neighbourhood}}\max_{\Gamma_A}q.
\]
The inequality from below follows from the maximum principle. If $q(x)$ is finite, USC supplies a neighbourhood where $q<q(x)+\eta$, and an affinoid neighbourhood therein gives the reverse inequality as $\eta\to0$. If $q(x)=-\infty$, use every finite bound instead. Thus values on the union of ALL these Shilov boundaries determine pointwise weights and their order.

There is also a Hartogs upper lemma. Suppose classical psh $q_j$ are defined near compact $Q$ and $h$ is finite continuous. If $\limsup_jq_j(\xi)\leq h(\xi)$ for every Shilov point of every sufficiently small affinoid neighbourhood, then eventually $q_j\leq h+\eta$ on $Q$. Choose a finite affinoid cover of $Q$ on each member of which the oscillation of $h$ is less than $\eta/3$. Each finite Shilov boundary has all $q_j(\xi)\leq h(\xi)+\eta/3$ eventually; one late index works for the finite cover. The maximum principle then gives the assertion (with room in the constants). The same proof works for a net using finite directed upper bounds. This is upper control only.

Wanner, arXiv:1801.04713v3, 8 November2018, Theorem4.7, states that a continuous function on an open subset of a smooth PROPER algebraic curve over a complete ALGEBRAICALLY CLOSED NONTRIVIALLY VALUED field is Thuillier-subharmonic if and only if its CLD Hessian current is positive. Properness is the standing hypothesis of Section4, explicitly checked at LF793--810. Its full immediate six-step proof was read, together with Definitions2.4,3.18 and the necessary smooth recognition/pullback results3.20--21 and approximation4.6. ROOT394's minimality bridge on those curve tests is valid at exactly these hypotheses. GR's all-extension definition avoids limiting classical recognition to these algebraic tests. Neither theorem transports the surface energy/current identity to a larger field or proves that ambient divisor tests recover all tests on an arbitrary curve.

The retained ROOT394 bridge itself has a short independent proof. Our local weight charts are open torus analytifications, so smooth ambient psh weights pull back to smooth psh weights on the stated algebraic curve tests by Wanner3.21, including after the stated field extension. Among finite continuous ambient functions, those whose pullbacks have positive curve Hessian currents form a sheaf closed under local uniform limits: uniform pullback convergence and continuous coefficient/current differentiation give weak Hessian convergence, and positivity is closed. This sheaf contains the smooth psh weights, so minimality contains every stage of P. Wanner4.7 recognizes these CONTINUOUS curve pullbacks. The decreasing extended-weight conclusion follows from the GR decreasing closure at those same curve tests, including the identically-minus-infinite case. This uses functorial pullback of functions and smooth tropicalizations, not a base-change formula for surface products or energy.

The separation and compactness gates therefore remain. We have not shown that $DD((u-v)\delta_{\operatorname{div}P})=0$ implies that every curve pullback of $u-v$ is harmonic, or that zero pairings determine an actual generated difference pointwise modulo constants. Such an argument must prove the divisor restriction, test-extension and any base-change steps; unbounded differences additionally need divisor integrability and null-set removability. Shilov reconstruction would identify weights if equality on ALL its boundary values were proved, but equal MA supplies no such equality yet. Upper boundary control supplies neither lower control nor uniform integrability of a general energy sublevel. These are precise unresolved steps, not claimed counterexamples to P16.7.
